shipment.title: Shipment-claim scheduler-baseline marker (enabling precondition)
shipment.description:
## Bootstrap prerequisite (chain root, marker producer) — do NOT auto-claim

`154-S`/`173-F` produces the scheduler-baseline marker and is now the **root of
the remaining predecessor chain** `154-S → 176-S → 157-S..169-S`. Its governed
prerequisite `155-S` (`154-S depends_on 155-S`, DAG-root correction commit
`69e900be`) has **SHIPPED** (implementation PR #450, merge `2c8759c3`; closure
PR #451, `main` `c57185c1`; `155-S` and all 45 manifest items — `174-F` + 44
tasks — archived), so that edge is satisfied and retained as provenance only.

The marker does not exist at `154-S`'s own claim time and `173-F` is internally
multi-wave, so claiming it activates all members **unmarked** → standard P-002.6
admission halts `WAVE_NO_PROGRESS`. It runs only as an operator-supervised
bootstrap (drive `173-F` members green in declared dependency order without the
strict active-residual halt). With `155-S` complete, `154-S` is the **only
remaining** shipment of the bounded bootstrap set originally recorded as
{`155-S`, `154-S`}; every later shipment uses the marked-aware scheduler.

**Waiver status: APPROVED (CONDITIONAL) — 2026-09-28.** The operator approved
the `154-S` active-residual halt bypass with conditions (accepted verbatim
2026-09-28T19:42 -07:00: "And with that, I think we should move forward with the
remaining recommended decisions."). Conditions: (1) covers `154-S` only; (2)
stash `C29EBEE5` re-validation MUST PASS first; (3) supervised bootstrap with
nothing else active; (4) skips ONLY the active-residual halt — local review, CI,
Copilot review and merge-commit rules all still apply, no admin bypass. Label
`bootstrap-bypass-unapproved` was replaced by
`bootstrap-bypass-approved-conditional`.

**Gate: `C29EBEE5` — SATISFIED 2026-09-29; bootstrap hold RELEASED.**
Plan-review attempt 7 (2026-09-29) returned ADVISORY (no P0/P1), and the
operator recorded `operator_authorization: approved` for it
(2026-09-29T14:40:58-07:00, verbatim "C29EBEE5 gate approved", relayed by the
Orchestrator; recorded in the plan's attempt-7 `## Plan Review`). Stage then ran
the plan's `## Harvest Checklist` (branch `stage/173f-harvest`), archived stash
`C29EBEE5`, and removed only `do-not-claim-until-convergence`.
`bootstrap-bypass-approved-conditional` stays: the waiver conditions above
(1), (3) and (4) still bind the supervised bootstrap run; condition (2) is met
by this gate.

**Attempt 5 (FAIL).** Plan-review attempt 5 found F1–F8 (P1/P2): stale
`173-F` contracts against the post-`174-F` code. Details are in
`docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md`.

**Option A decided.** The operator decided F2 on 2026-09-28T22:22 -07:00
("Decision: option A"). The marker is kept through block, unblock and
`ReturnBlockedItem`. An item is claim-activated only if all three hold:

* its status is `active`;
* its marker equals the active shipment's ID;
* it is in that shipment's manifest.

Recorded in
`docs/decisions/2026-09-28-173f-marker-lifecycle-option-a-decision.md`.

**Attempt 6 (FAIL).** Stage re-planned `173-F` under option A:

* new units U0c and U1b (claim-crash recovery accepts this shipment's
  marker);
* F1–F8 remediated;
* re-hardened.

Plan-review attempt 6 (six personas, `dispatch_mode: multi-agent-dispatch`)
returned **FAIL**:

* one P1: U0b (`173.007-T`) must be a dependency of U1 (`173.001-T`), because
  U1 turns it green;
* ten P2s, including:
  * U1b acceptance-criteria precision;
  * a claim-crash scenario (U4(2)) that cannot be executed;
  * revert guidance;
  * U5 depending on U4;
  * the manifest JSON path;
  * the index-backed R3;
  * error-class injection;
  * a mixed-binary rollout checkpoint;
  * the learning waiver.

Attempts 5 and 6 are two consecutive FAILs, so the plan-review circuit
breaker tripped and it was escalated (P-013.6). The harvest was **not**
updated at that point (superseded by the 2026-09-29 harvest below).

**Attempt 7 (ADVISORY, 2026-09-29).** Operator-authorized past the circuit
breaker. All attempt-6 findings were resolved. The operator-required size
validation found the plan too large for one supervised bootstrap (9 tasks, at
least 7 waves) and decomposed it:

* bootstrap slice for `154-S`: 7 tasks in 5 waves (`173.006-T`, `173.007-T`,
  new U0c, new U1b, `173.001-T`, `173.003-T`, `173.005-T`);
* `173.002-T` (U2) retired into `173.007-T`; archived from `queued` at
  harvest;
* `173.004-T` (U4) deferred to a new follow-on feature, with no new shipment.

Six personas returned ADVISORY with five P2s, and the text remediation was
applied in the plan. Details are in the plan's attempt-7 `## Plan Review`.

**Harvest (2026-09-29, plan `## Harvest Checklist`).** Operator-authorized
(`operator_authorization: approved`). Applied:

* follow-on feature `182-F` ("Scheduler-baseline marker: option A lifecycle
  regression net (173-F follow-on)") created; `173.004-T` had its
  `173.002-T` edge removed, was adopted under `182-F` as **`182.001-T`**, and
  carries the deferred U4 contract. **No follow-on shipment.** `182.001-T`
  keeps `blocks` edges onto `173.001-T` and `173.003-T` and is routed only
  under the 074-DL rule after `154-S` ships;
* `173.002-T` (U2) retired into `173.007-T`: `173.005-T` → `173.002-T` edge
  removed, supersession provenance recorded, removed from this manifest and
  archived **directly from `queued`** (`archived_status: queued`). Release
  scope is flat, so the ship gate no longer evaluates it; archival keeps this
  omitted child terminal so `173-F` can complete;
* new tasks `173.008-T` (U0c, RED claim-crash recovery harness) and
  `173.009-T` (U1b, claim recovery accepts this shipment's marker);
* edges added: `173.009-T` → `173.008-T`; `173.001-T` → `173.009-T`;
  `173.001-T` → `173.007-T` (attempt-6 P1-1, U0b → U1); `173.003-T` →
  `173.009-T`; `173.005-T` → `173.007-T`, `173.001-T`, `173.003-T`. Edge
  removed: `173.003-T` → `173.006-T` (now transitive through `173.001-T`);
* contracts of `173.001-T`, `173.003-T`, `173.005-T`, `173.006-T`,
  `173.007-T` and the `173-F` description rewritten to the option A plan
  text.

**Manifest (bootstrap slice, 7 tasks in 5 waves).** `173-F`, then:

1. wave 1: `173.006-T` (U0a), `173.007-T` (U0b), `173.008-T` (U0c);
2. wave 2: `173.009-T` (U1b);
3. wave 3: `173.001-T` (U1);
4. wave 4: `173.003-T` (U3, incl. the `-race` shipment regression gate);
5. wave 5: `173.005-T` (U5).

**Pre-ship check for Ship (Harvest Checklist step 7).** At ship time, no child
of `173-F` outside this manifest may be non-terminal. Expected state: the only
non-manifest child is `173.002-T`, archived from `queued`
(`archived_status: queued`). Shipment release scope is flat (an explicit
feature member does not expand to its descendants), so the ship gate does not
evaluate `173.002-T`; it must stay terminal so the listed `173-F` can
complete. The adopted U4 is no longer a
child of `173-F` (it is `182.001-T` under `182-F`). If any other non-manifest
`173-F` child is non-terminal, stop and return to Stage.

`154-S` may now be routed to Ship as the operator-supervised bootstrap under the
conditional waiver, subject to the `182-S` shipped-provenance guard below
(satisfied: `182-S` is `archived` with `archived_status: shipped`, merge
`70d72044`) and nothing else active.

**Flake prerequisite: `182-S` must ship first (operator decision 2026-09-28).**
`154-S` holds a `blocks` edge onto the new single-member shipment `182-S`:

* `182-S` carries task `181.001-T` under feature `181-F`;
* the fix makes the UR3 crash-ready handoff tolerate a partial marker;
* it covers stash `BDA56ED8`, with duplicate `46A898B8` archived.

The fix is covered by the flake plan
`docs/exec-plans/2026-09-28-ur3-crash-ready-handoff-flake-plan.md`
(plan-review attempt 2 PASS).

Task-level `blocks` edges onto `181.001-T` also exist from `173.001-T`,
`173.003-T` and `173.006-T` (and from the archived `173.002-T` and the adopted
`182.001-T`, formerly `173.004-T`), retained as provenance; `181.001-T` has
shipped. The new `173.008-T`/`173.009-T` need no such edge. There is no
known-flake rerun waiver.

**Shipped-provenance guard for `182-S` (manual policy until `AF1E5075`).**
The `blocks` edge onto `182-S` does NOT by itself enforce "must ship first":

* queue dependency resolution (`filterByResolvedDependencies`, via
  `IsNoLongerBlockingStatus`) stops blocking on ANY of the six cascade
  terminal statuses (`done`, `accepted`, `archived`, `shipped`, `abandoned`,
  `rejected`);
* `ClaimShipment` performs no dependency validation at all.

So `154-S` may be routed only when `182-S` has **shipped provenance**: live
`status: shipped`, or `status: archived` with `archived_status: shipped`, read
from the Markdown source (the index does not project `archived_status`). If
`182-S` reaches any other terminal status, `154-S` stays held even though the
edge reads as resolved. This is the same manual-policy framing as the post-ship
rule below. It is not an automated check, and it is in addition to the
`C29EBEE5` gate (satisfied 2026-09-29).

**Routing hold (RELEASED 2026-09-29).** With `155-S` shipped, `154-S` has no
unshipped predecessor, so the Orchestrator's status + dependency eligibility
gate no longer holds it, and the current Orchestrator/Ship contracts do not read
labels. The bootstrap hold label `do-not-claim-until-convergence` was released
by the satisfied `C29EBEE5` gate (attempt-7 ADVISORY +
`operator_authorization: approved`) under the approved conditional waiver, not
by convergence (which `154-S` itself enables), and was removed at the
2026-09-29 harvest. `154-S` still runs ONLY as the operator-supervised
bootstrap under `bootstrap-bypass-approved-conditional` (nothing else active;
only the active-residual halt is skipped) and MUST NOT be routed through an
unsupervised dark-mode scope.
Label-aware claim refusal is tracked as deferred stash `AF1E5075`.

**After `154-S` ships (074-DL).** `141-S`, `147-S`, `152-S`, `153-S`, `176-S`,
`177-S`, `178-S`, `179-S` hold `blocks` edges onto `154-S`; those edges release
on ANY terminal status of `154-S` and no agent contract yet checks shipped
provenance or marker consumption. Until `AF1E5075` delivers that contract, the
Orchestrator MUST NOT route anything behind `154-S` unless `154-S` has shipped
provenance (`status: shipped`, or `archived` with `archived_status: shipped`,
read from Markdown source) AND an operator attestation comment on `154-S`
confirms the external autoharness scheduler is consuming the marker. This is a
manual policy, not an automated check. (`backlogit update` on an archived
record now preserves `archived_from`/`archived_status` — fixed by `842b701d`/
`e09befa8`, pinned by `internal/core/archive_update_provenance_test.go` — but
the provenance read must still use Markdown source because the index does not
project `archived_status`.)

Waiver provenance (factual): the conditional approval above is recorded as an
operator comment event on `154-S` (2026-09-28T19:45 -07:00, actor "operator
(relayed by Orchestrator)"); that event log (`.backlogit/logs/154-S.jsonl`) is
local and git-ignored, so this banner, the Stage memory
`docs/memory/2026-09-28/stage-triage-513e62ab-fb0a850b-memory.md`, and PR #455
are the tracked record. Earlier history: Ship's `155-S` bootstrap records
describe the original operator authorization as scoped to the bounded set
{`155-S`, `154-S`} and exercised for `155-S` only —
`docs/memory/2026-09-20/155-s-wave-1-quality-gate-blocker.md` (lines 15-18) and
the `waiver` field of `.backlogit/checkpoints/checkpoint-20260920-234325.json`;
`.backlogit/reconcile/155-S-pre-20260920T233209Z.md` records the `155-S` waiver
itself as operator-approved. See
`docs/decisions/2026-09-20-shipment-claim-wave-scheduler-convergence-deliberation.md`
("Bootstrap Resolution").

members.title: Shipment-claim scheduler-baseline marker (enabling precondition)
members.description:
Covering feature for CC0EBB59 (re-validated via stash C29EBEE5). ENABLING PRECONDITION, not full defect resolution: adds an additive, backward-compatible scheduler-baseline marker — the single custom_fields key scheduler_baseline_claim, value = activating shipment ID — written by ClaimShipment on every manifest member whose preimage status was queued, so a claim-activated manifest task can be told apart from an organic active residual. The observable P-002.6 misclassification is resolved only once the out-of-workspace autoharness scheduler consumes the marker.

Option A lifecycle (operator decision 2026-09-28, docs/decisions/2026-09-28-173f-marker-lifecycle-option-a-decision.md): the marker is kept through block, unblock, ReturnBlockedItem, ship, abandon, normalize and generic writes; it is removed only by rollback (exact preimage restore). Consumer predicate (normative, published by U5): an item is claim-activated iff status == active AND its marker == the ID of the currently active shipment AND it is in that shipment's current items manifest; "non-empty => claim-activated" is withdrawn.

Plan: docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md. Review: plan-review attempt 7 ADVISORY (no P0/P1), operator_authorization: approved 2026-09-29T14:40:58-07:00 ("C29EBEE5 gate approved", relayed by the Orchestrator); harvested 2026-09-29 per the plan's Harvest Checklist.

Bootstrap slice shipped by 154-S (7 tasks, 5 waves): wave 1 173.006-T (U0a), 173.007-T (U0b, absorbs retired U2), 173.008-T (U0c); wave 2 173.009-T (U1b, recovery accepts this shipment's marker; lands before U1); wave 3 173.001-T (U1, marker write); wave 4 173.003-T (U3, rollback verification + -race regression gate); wave 5 173.005-T (U5, marker contract doc). In-repo scope: internal/core/shipment_lifecycle.go (claim loop, marker write, shared key constant), internal/core/shipment_recovery.go (U1b), tests in internal/core, internal/cli and internal/mcp, and one operator doc. No other shipment lifecycle operation and no generic write path is changed.

Decomposition at harvest: 173.002-T (U2) retired into 173.007-T and archived from queued (archived_status: queued) and removed from the 154-S manifest; shipment release scope is flat, so archival keeps this omitted child terminal and 173-F can complete. 173.004-T (U4, option A lifecycle regression net) deferred: adopted as 182.001-T under follow-on feature 182-F, no follow-on shipment; routed only under the 074-DL rule after 154-S ships.

members.title: RED harness: claim marking (activation, re-claim, ordering)
members.description:
U0a [CC0EBB59 / C29EBEE5] RED harness + characterization, claim marking. Contract rewritten to the option A plan text at the 173-F harvest (2026-09-29, plan Harvest Checklist step 5); supersedes the pre-option-A contract. Source: docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md (U0a, attempt 7). Wave 1 of the 154-S bootstrap slice.

Domain: tests. File: internal/core/shipment_claim_marker_test.go (new). Written before U1 (173.001-T). No 173-F dependencies (the 181.001-T edge is retained as provenance; 181.001-T shipped in 182-S). 3 scenarios. Execution posture: test-first (RED).

RED-compile rule: use the literal string "scheduler_baseline_claim", never the schedulerBaselineClaimKey constant (it arrives in U1b). Test-seam rule: no t.Parallel when swapping a package-global seam; restore via t.Cleanup. Fixture rule: no non-queued member-parent that has queued member children.

(1) RED. ClaimShipment sets scheduler_baseline_claim = <shipmentID> on every member whose preimage status is queued. Fixture includes a queued member whose preimage already carries a stale foreign marker ("OLD-S"); after the claim its value is the new shipment ID (re-claim overwrite). Fixture includes a queued member whose preimage has other non-empty custom_fields; those keys survive unchanged (two-value presence assertions, v, ok := m[key]). Members that are not queued (e.g. already active or done) are byte-identical to their preimage. The shipment artifact differs from its preimage only in status and updated_at.
(2) RED, ordering (F5). The manifest lists a queued child before its queued member-parent ([child, parent]), so the bounded cascade activates the parent before the loop reaches it. Both child and parent end up marked. One pair suffices because the claim loop walks the ordered manifest slice; if a marking loop ever ranges over a map or set, use at least 5 independent pairs.
(3) Characterization, NOT RED. A non-claim setArtifactStatus caller (e.g. a queue move) produces byte-identical frontmatter before and after. The fixture's preimage carries a stale blocked_reason, so the existing clearStaleBlockedReason behavior is characterized too.

AC: (1) and (2) fail against pre-implementation code; (3) passes both before and after the implementation and is not counted as RED; no production file modified.

members.title: RED harness: claim-marker external read surface (absorbs retired U2)
members.description:
U0b [CC0EBB59 / C29EBEE5] RED harness + characterization, external read surface and consumer recipe; ABSORBS the retired U2 (173.002-T, archived from queued at this harvest). Contract rewritten to the option A plan text at the 173-F harvest (2026-09-29, plan Harvest Checklist step 5). Source: docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md (U0b, attempt 7). Wave 1 of the 154-S bootstrap slice.

Domain: tests. Files: one test file in internal/cli and one in internal/mcp (one fixture helper per package: cli_test, mcp). Written before U1 (173.001-T depends on this task — attempt 6 P1-1). No 173-F dependencies. 3 scenarios. Execution posture: test-first (RED). RED-compile rule: use the literal string "scheduler_baseline_claim". Test-seam rule: no t.Parallel when swapping a package-global seam; restore via t.Cleanup.

Each RED scenario walks the EXACT U5 recipe paths on one transport, after a real claim of a shipment with one queued member:
(1) RED, CLI (frontmatter-backed item read). backlogit shipment list --status active --format json returns a JSON array of length 1; .[0].id is the shipment ID; .[0].custom_fields.items[] contains the member ID; backlogit get <member> --format json has .custom_fields.scheduler_baseline_claim == <shipmentID>.
(2) RED, MCP (index-backed). backlogit_list_shipments {"status":"active"} returns an array of length 1 with the same .[0].custom_fields.items[]; backlogit_get_item for the member has the identical .custom_fields.scheduler_baseline_claim value.
(3) Characterization. Before any claim, shipment list --status active returns a present empty array [] (not null, not missing) on both transports, and the key is absent on both transports for an organic-active item (two-value presence assertion). Written as t.Run subtests in each package's file.

AC: (1) and (2) fail before U1 (marker absent) and pass after it; (3) passes before and after; fewer than 4 scenarios. Post-implementation AC (from retired U2): the marker reaches both transports through the existing generic custom_fields projection (CLI internal/cli/get.go buildDetailMap; MCP internal/db/queries.go scanArtifactRow, fed by UpsertItem, which persistArtifact calls after the file write in the same call); no bespoke projection field, no marker-specific filter, no read helper, and no state mutation is added.

members.title: RED harness: claim crash recovery with marked members (U0c)
members.description:
U0c [CC0EBB59 / C29EBEE5] RED harness + characterization, claim crash recovery with marked members (F1/F4). Created at the 173-F harvest (2026-09-29, plan Harvest Checklist step 4). Contract per docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md (U0c, attempt 7). Wave 1 of the 154-S bootstrap slice.

Domain: tests. File: internal/core/shipment_claim_marker_recovery_test.go (new). No 173-F dependencies (does not depend on U1). 3 scenarios. Execution posture: test-first (RED).

RED-compile rule: use the literal string "scheduler_baseline_claim", never the schedulerBaselineClaimKey constant (it only arrives in U1b). Test-seam rule: no t.Parallel when swapping a package-global seam; restore via t.Cleanup.

Fixture mechanism: fabricate the crashed state directly — a shipment-operation/v1 claim INTENT journal (the only phase recovery reconciles, shipment_recovery.go reconcileShipmentLifecycleIntent) with its preimage, plus current member files — via in-package calls to writeShipmentLifecycleJournalForWorkspace and persistArtifact under withShipmentOperation (governed ctx for the shipment's active write). Close the original workspace before reopening with NewWorkspace (Windows SQLite and temp-dir cleanup).

(1) RED. Crash after marking: the shipment is active and every preimage-queued member is active + marked with the journal's shipment ID. Fixture includes one member whose PREIMAGE carries a stale foreign marker ("OLD-S"); after rollback its value is "OLD-S" again, byte-for-byte. recoverPendingShipmentOperations, invoked through a fresh NewWorkspace open, rolls back successfully; every member and the shipment are byte-identical to the preimage (no marker key where the preimage had none; custom_fields nil if it was nil before the claim). A following ClaimShipment of the same shipment succeeds (nothing wedged). A direct assertion checks that the last claim candidate returned by memberRecoveryCandidates carries the journal's marker.
(2) RED. Double-fault partial compensation: the shipment is already restored to its queued preimage; one member is restored and another is still active + marked. Recovery succeeds and converges to the preimage.
(3) Characterization, NOT RED. A member carrying a marker whose value differs from BOTH the preimage's own value and journal.ShipmentID (or otherwise diverged) still fails closed with ErrShipmentConflict (guards against over-broad acceptance).

AC: (1) and (2) fail today with ErrShipmentConflict (the genuine RED for the recovery surface); (3) passes before and after and is not counted as RED; fewer than 4 scenarios; no production file modified.

members.title: Claim recovery accepts this shipment's marker (U1b)
members.description:
U1b [CC0EBB59 / C29EBEE5] Claim-recovery marker compatibility (F1). Created at the 173-F harvest (2026-09-29, plan Harvest Checklist step 4). Contract per docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md (U1b, attempt 7). Wave 2 of the 154-S bootstrap slice. U1b lands BEFORE U1 (173.001-T): at no commit may the marker be written while claim crash recovery still rejects marked members (the F1 wedge).

Domain: code. Files: internal/core/shipment_recovery.go, plus the one shared constant line in internal/core/shipment_lifecycle.go. Depends on U0c (173.008-T). Execution posture: test-first (turn U0c GREEN); careful mode (recovery CAS change).

Declare const schedulerBaselineClaimKey = "scheduler_baseline_claim" in internal/core/shipment_lifecycle.go, next to ClaimShipment (the producer). U1 reuses it. No other change to that file in U1b.

In memberRecoveryCandidates, the rollback+claim case for a preimage-queued member returns three candidates, in this order:
1. the preimage (it may carry a stale marker, R1);
2. preimage + Status=Active, marker as in the preimage (the intermediate member-parent cascade window, kept so rollback CAS accepts it);
3. preimage + Status=Active + custom_fields.scheduler_baseline_claim = journal.ShipmentID, LAST. Build custom_fields as a fresh map copy of the preimage's map (nil -> new one-entry map).
The marked target is last: validateShipmentLifecycleRecoveryOutcome uses candidates[len-1] for committed evidence and candidates[0] for compensated evidence. For claim the committed-evidence path is defensive only (claim emits no correlation-tagged evidence events and claim recovery rolls back before any terminal evidence is appended). Nothing changes for non-queued preimage members, for the shipment candidates, or for the block, unblock and normalize cases (option A). Errors wrap with %w; keep the ErrShipmentConflict sentinel.

AC: U0c (1) and (2) turn GREEN and U0c (3) stays GREEN; existing recovery and UR3 tests stay green; the marker values accepted on a member are ONLY the preimage's own value (candidates 1 and 2) or journal.ShipmentID on the marked-last candidate (candidate 3) — any other value fails closed with ErrShipmentConflict.

members.title: Persist scheduler-baseline marker on claim activation (explicit claimMarker writer)
members.description:
U1 [CC0EBB59 / C29EBEE5] Persist the marker on claim activation. Contract rewritten to the option A plan text at the 173-F harvest (2026-09-29, plan Harvest Checklist step 5); supersedes the pre-option-A contract (activatedIDs rollback tracking no longer exists). Source: docs/exec-plans/2026-09-13-shipment-claim-scheduler-reconciliation-plan.md (U1, attempt 7) and docs/decisions/2026-09-28-173f-marker-lifecycle-option-a-decision.md. Wave 3 of the 154-S bootstrap slice.

Domain: code. File: internal/core/shipment_lifecycle.go. Depends on U0a (173.006-T), U0b (173.007-T, attempt 6 P1-1) and U1b (173.009-T); the 181.001-T edge is retained as provenance. Execution posture: test-first (turn U0a/U0b GREEN). Reuse the schedulerBaselineClaimKey constant declared by U1b.

Marker contract (pinned): single custom_fields key scheduler_baseline_claim; value = activating shipment ID (non-empty string). Reserved but not write-protected; consumers rely on the three-part predicate, never on the raw value alone.

Seam form: explicit per-call parameter, not a context value. Extract the body of setArtifactStatus into an unexported writer taking a claimMarker string argument; setArtifactStatus calls it with "" (behavior unchanged); the ClaimShipment claim loop calls it with the shipment ID; the seam is never visible to MoveShipmentStatus or other downstream writes. (A shared applyClaimActivation helper with U1b was rejected; only the key constant is shared.)

Ordering-independent marking (F5): for each member whose preimage status is queued, the write sets Status=Active and the key in ONE persistArtifact call. If the member is already active (a member-parent the bounded cascade activated earlier in the loop), the writer still persists the key as a marker-only write: no status transition, no parent cascade, no status_changed event (unaudited; documented in U5). If the key already equals the shipment ID, the marker-only write is a no-op (no persist), compared on the artifact as loadArtifact returns it (index-first). A marker-only write bumps UpdatedAt (recovery candidates 2 and 3 already set ignoreUpdatedAt). The extracted writer keeps every existing side effect of setArtifactStatus (clearStaleBlockedReason, event append, bounded cascade). custom_fields: omitempty applies to the whole map; set the key explicitly and lazily initialize a nil map. A re-claim overwrites a stale value (including another shipment's).

Parent-cascade safety: cascadePersistedParentStatuses (bounded by shipmentMemberCascadeBoundaryContextKey) never writes the key; non-member parents are neither mutated nor marked; member-parents are marked only by the loop. Rollback coupling: covered by the existing journaled preimage plus snapshotShipArtifacts / restoreShipArtifactsDetailed (exact-byte restore); no compensating marker write is added (F3). No other lifecycle operation (Block, Unblock, ReturnBlocked, Ship, normalize, Abandon) and no generic write path is changed (option A).

AC: U0a (1)(2) and U0b (1)(2) turn GREEN; U0a (3) and U0b (3) stay GREEN; the key is set exactly on preimage-queued manifest members; non-claim setArtifactStatus callers are byte-identical; non-member parents are not marked; consumers that ignore the key see no behavior change (pinned by U0a (3) byte-identity and U0b (3) key absence).
